detail.abstract: Upon establishing direct-to-consumer e-commerce channels, imported consumer goods brands commonly face price inversion and distribution conflicts that cannot be effectively coordinated by conventional single-wholesale-price contracts. A data-driven computational framework is developed by integrating a two-stage Stackelberg game with parameter calibration and numerical simulation. The model incorporates cross-price elasticity, consumer channel preference and offline service spillover, and computes equilibrium prices and profit allocations under decentralised, centralised and contractual coordination scenarios. A revenue-sharing-service-cost-sharing contract is then designed and evaluated through computer-based numerical and Monte Carlo simulations. Parameters are calibrated using 72 months of operating records, including 2.186 million SKU-level transactions, data from 350 distributors and service records from 150 outlets. Calibrated counterfactual results indicate that decentralised decision-making generates a 19.4% profit loss relative to the centralised benchmark, while contractual coordination increases simulated supply chain profit by 14.2%, with brand-owner and distributor profits increasing by 11.6% and 17.3%, respectively. When the revenue-sharing ratio is maintained within [0.62, 0.71], coordination is achieved. Monte Carlo simulation with 5,000 parameter sets yields an effectiveness rate of 87.6%, confirming the computational robustness of the proposed coordination mechanism.

detail.abstract:
A national terminology service can meet every requirement placed on it (high availability, low latency, a complete and correctly versioned history) and still sit at the centre of a health system whose consumers act on incompatible meanings. This paper argues that semantic availability is an end-to-end property in the sense of the end-to-end argument in distributed systems design: it is produced jointly by the authoritative service, the distribution mechanism, and every consuming system, and cannot therefore be assured by component-level requirements alone. The term semantic availability is borrowed from an earlier dependability literature, which defined it for a single dynamic data feed whose fault model is an unreasonable value from a source with no adequate specification.

The case examined here inverts both halves: the specification is published, versioned, and governed, and the failing value is entirely reasonable, having been rendered wrong by a governing context that moved while the data did not. Invariant-based detection is poorly placed to reach such a failure, because the violated invariant cannot be inferred from the unchanged feed alone.

The paper sets out four layers at which the property can fail. For the distribution-facing layer, it defines a family of measures, version-convergence availability, which reports separately on releases applied by their deadline and on the incoherence still standing when a period ends. A three-quarter worked example shows why both estate-level numbers are needed: they diverge, and the first cannot be computed at all in a quarter with no deadline in it. The paper then states the architectural properties a distribution contract must carry and tests the account against the WHO and ITU draft Reference Architecture Guidance for Digital Public Infrastructure for Health. That draft carries real normative obligations on both sides (publishing duties on the terminology service, and a duty on two components to subscribe) and lists further enabling capabilities in a non-normative appendix. What no part of it establishes is a continuity-and-recovery contract by which an identified consumer can demonstrate that it holds an identified applicable release and can be returned to a known-good state when it does not.

detail.abstract: The integration of generative AI into accounting and finance practice has intensified a longstanding professional obligation to exercise independent judgment and take responsibility for analytical conclusions. Large language models are prone to producing plausible but incorrect outputs, yet professionals remain accountable for decisions informed by those outputs. This accountability creates an educational challenge: preparing graduates to critically evaluate AIgenerated analyses, identify errors, and take professional responsibility for their conclusions. The challenge is compounded by the verification paradox, in which students are expected to evaluate AI-generated content concerning material they are still mastering. This paper presents an AIassisted pedagogical platform designed to address this paradox by asking students to evaluate AI-generated reports containing deliberately seeded errors, an approach we term adversarial pedagogy. Using a design science research framework, the paper examines the platform's design principles, pilot evaluation, and implications for accounting education.

detail.abstract: Agentic payments have a measurement literature and a leaderboard culture, but no one measures the control layer: the small set of facilitator operators through whom x402 settlement routes, and the accountability structure of the composition chain those operators sit in. This paper reports the first such measurement across the three chains carrying materially all x402 activity (Base, Polygon, Solana), porting the gateway- concentration method developed for stablecoin routing. Five results organize the paper. Settlement-layer concentration exceeds the stablecoin gateway layer it sits on: July 2026 facilitator HHIs measure 6,512 by payment count and 4,700 by corrected dollar volume on Base, 4,071 and 3,831 on Solana, Polygon is effectively single-operator, and every reading clears the merger-guidelines highly-concentrated thresholds (1,800 current; 2,500 superseded) at a market age under fourteen months. The count layer and the value layer have different monopolists, on two chains independently, so single-metric concentration claims are structurally fragile. Headline counts are dominated by subsidized and self-referential pipelines, which buyer cardinality exposes without any wash-trading heuristic. At the value layer the market is pre-material (corrected cross-chain July volume of $583,430; measured against its own settlement rails in May, the validated baseline month, four ten-millionths of the USDC transfer value it settles on) yet already message- significant (2.83 percent of May USDC transfer events). And the composition chain that delivers an agentic payment has no layer at which accountability composes: settlement is irreversible by design, the facilitator sits outside both the AI-governance and payments-regulation perimeters, and top sell-side endpoints are pseudonymous even to full-data analysis. A methodological result conditions all of the above: published measurements of this market diverge by an order of magnitude, for reasons that reduce to attribution-set and filter choices.

detail.abstract: Digital systems increasingly delegate the resolution of persons, organizations, products, places, and documents to language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and autonomous agents. Yet recognizing identical character strings is not equivalent to resolving identical entities. This study synthesizes research on entity linking, entity matching, temporally evolving knowledge bases, RAG, and multi-agent LLM systems with public enterprise data-quality surveys from 2020-2026. It demonstrates that identity decisions break down across four analytical zones: identity collapse under name ambiguity and popularity bias, semantic fragmentation across data silos, temporal discontinuity of changing entities, and the semantic vulnerability of retrieval context. These are not four isolated defects. In RAG architectures, they can cascade from indexing through retrieval to generation, whereas in agentic systems, an earlier misidentification can alter the target of the subsequent step, the next query, and even the purported verification. While economic evidence cannot be converted into a universal cost for a single entity error, it consistently documents the substantial operational scale of the problem: Gartner reports a historical average of at least USD 12.9 million per year attributable to poor data quality and predicts the abandonment of 60% of AI projects unsupported by AI-ready data by the end of 2026. In the Monte Carlo/Wakefield sample, two-thirds of respondents reported in 2024 a data incident costing at least USD 100,000 during the preceding six months; in the 2025 Fivetran/Redpoint sample, 42% of enterprises stated that more than half of their AI projects had been delayed, underperforming, or unsuccessful because of data readiness. The concluding theoretical section examines Daniel Beránek's Digital Identity Optimization (DIO) and Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI) as a novel framework for governing the integrity of digital identity in environments where the entity is reconstructed from fragmented, temporally variable, and mutually conflicting representations. Its empirical validation constitutes a subsequent phase of development, not a precondition for the existence of the problem itself or for the legitimacy of the framework. DIO is strongest precisely where the entity is not a single record, but a temporally, multilingually, and infrastructurally dispersed configuration of relations.

detail.abstract: Generative and agentic AI significantly lower the cost of producing plausible artifacts for operational decision-making, from analyses and recommendations to pricing suggestions and what-if simulations. This article argues that the resulting operations problem is not simply more output. It is cognitive work-in-process (cognitive WIP): the accumulation of AI-enabled artifacts that require evaluation before they can inform action, enter workflows, or be discarded. We define the discernment gap as a capacity mismatch: AI increases the volume, variety, and provenance ambiguity of candidate artifacts, while evaluation capacity remains scarce, unevenly distributed, and endogenously allocated. The article develops this argument in four steps. First, we distinguish AI-enabled artifact flow from earlier forms of information overload. Second, we specify a process model of the discernment gap and identify its boundary conditions. Third, we introduce lean curation as a process-design discipline for managing cognitive WIP through admission control, evaluation at the source, calibrated routing, evaluative memory, and attention governance. Finally, we outline curation modes and research opportunities for studying evaluation capacity, review-policy design, and learning from evaluation traces. The core claim is that generative and agentic AI shift the unit of analysis from model output to the artifact lifecycle: how artifacts are generated, routed, evaluated, acted on, monitored, stored, and retired.

detail.abstract: Livestreaming platforms record creator speech, viewer chat, audience size, and paid support within the same session, allowing analysts to construct cross-side relational measures. Such measures can rest on unequal amounts of usable trace information across sessions, complicating how their conventional associations should be interpreted. We study observed affective correspondence (OAC), the proximity between positivity and negativity profiles in creator speech and active-commenter chat. Using 921 YouTube Live sessions from 81 monetizationactive, revenue-ranked creators, we estimate within-creator associations between OAC and several engagement records. Higher OAC is associated with larger peak audiences, more chat, and more frequent paid messages. The paid-message occurrence estimate is near zero, while the value estimate is imprecise in the primary model and model-sensitive across specifications. In the recovered archive, 9.4% of messages carry a positivity score and 5.3% carry a negativity score, and these counts vary widely across sessions. Text-volume restrictions weaken the OAC associations with chat and peak audience. Holding dimension-specific scored-message counts fixed produces additional attenuation relative to an approximate classical-error benchmark for those two associations, whereas the paid-message diagnostics show less additional attenuation. These results indicate that relational measures built from platform traces should be interpreted together with how much information was used to construct them and where that information came from. The fixed-information analysis is an interpretive diagnostic, not a correction or identification strategy.

detail.abstract: Study selection is the most labour-intensive stage of a systematic review, and it is two jobs. The first is cutting tens of thousands of records to a screenable few. The second is deciding includeor-exclude on what remains. These need different tools, and we validate a recall-first pipeline pairing them. Recall-first means it is tuned and scored to retain eligible studies and defaults to include when in doubt. For volume reduction, a small human seed drives an active-learning ranker that reproduces and improves a deployed ranking worker. Screened top-down, it discards a median 86% of a low-prevalence pool (under 5% eligible) while retaining 95% of eligibles, turning a 40,000-record search into a few thousand. A statistical stopping rule, tested on 26 pools, tells a reviewer when that recall has most likely been reached. For the decision, a cascaded large-language-model (LLM) ensemble resolves the confident majority with a low-cost fivemodel core, escalates only low-agreement records, and meters real compute cost, tens to a few hundred dollars per review. In its recall-first configuration it recovers a median 98% of eligibles across 153 reviews spanning management corpora and public medical benchmarks. The ensemble alone is a poor volume-cutter, discarding only 35% of records at 95% recall, so ranking and classification are not interchangeable. We correct a base-rate pattern that collapses at scale, and map where recall fails, on reviews whose eligibility is orthogonal to topical relevance. Because models keep improving and falling in price, the durable contribution is the architecture and division of labour.

detail.abstract: A low scaling exponent estimated from realized variance may reflect latent spot-variance regularity, the observation scheme, or both. This paper holds the market, sample, state variables, rolling window, and inference conventions of Yang (2026) fixed and changes only the apparent-roughness functional. On the same Binance BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT one-minute tape from January 2020 through July 2026, I compare the original increment-variance slope on log realized variance (IV), the same slope after Jacod-style pre-averaging (PA), and the Cont-Das normalized p-variation diagnostic on realized-volatility levels (PV). The PA-IV gap is treated as estimator disagreement. IV and PA display similar negative level associations with absolute funding, but neither retains transition information after persistence is controlled. PV admits a unique root in 83.7% of BTC windows and 81.1% of ETH windows; its funding coefficient is weaker and is not statistically distinguishable from zero with month effects. The PA-IV gap is not systematically explained by funding in the rolling specifications. Non-overlapping blocks confirm that the result depends on both the functional and the funding summary. The evidence supports a bounded conclusion: funding indexes a persistent observation-level state, but the association is not invariant to every roughness functional and does not identify latent spot regularity, a causal leverage channel, or a trading rule.

title: When Technology Backfires: Behavior-Based Targeting in Marketing Channels
affiliations: Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU), Xi'an Jiaotong University (XJTU) and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: When Technology Backfires: Behavior-Based Targeting in Marketing Channels
detail.abstract: Digital technologies enable retailers to identify competitors' captive consumers from purchase histories and inform them about the focal product through behavior-based targeting (BBT). BBT facilitates consumer acquisition but may also intensify channel competition, complicating retailers' BBT adoption decisions and channel members' pricing adjustments. To address these issues, we develop a two-period game-theoretic model of two competing marketing channels, each comprising a manufacturer and an exclusive retailer. We find that neither retailer adopts BBT when the proportion of captive consumers is sufficiently low, whereas both retailers adopt it when the proportion is sufficiently high. At intermediate levels, an asymmetric equilibrium arises in which only one retailer adopts BBT despite channel symmetry. Unlike conventional competitive targeting, which intensifies price competition upon implementation, BBT can mitigate price competition in the second period (upon implementation) while intensifying it in the first period (before implementation). When only one retailer adopts BBT, the adopting channel benefits while the non-adopting channel suffers; when both retailers adopt BBT, a prisoner's dilemma arises and all channel members' profits decline. Consumer myopia, manufacturer-determined adoption, and uniform wholesale pricing make BBT adoption more attractive, increasing the likelihood of the prisoner's dilemma.

title: Disentangling Content Quality and Source Credibility in Brand Communities (BC): The Homophily–Likeability Pathway and Conditional Similarity Inflation Bias
affiliations: Xavier University, Concordia University and Thompson Rivers University

detail.title: Disentangling Content Quality and Source Credibility in Brand Communities (BC): The Homophily–Likeability Pathway and Conditional Similarity Inflation Bias
detail.abstract: This study examines how interpersonal mechanisms—specifically homophily (similarity) and likeability—influence the evaluation of user-generated content in brand communities (BC), thereby improving understanding of how these variables affect source credibility. It distinguishes between content quality (accuracy, relevance, timeliness) and source credibility (expertise, trustworthiness) and investigates the role of similarity inflation bias. Data were collected from 480 members of brand communities via an online survey. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test a hierarchical model linking homophily, likeability, source credibility, and content quality. Low- and high-homophily subgroups were compared to determine how this influenced the relationships under examination.Homophily strongly predicted likeability, significantly enhancing source credibility. Source credibility was the primary driver of content quality, whereas homophily influenced content quality only indirectly, through evaluations of source likeability and credibility. The comparison of high- and low-similarity groups found that similarity increased credibility and strengthened relational effects only among high-homophily members, indicating a conditional similarity inflation bias. The study disentangled content quality from source credibility, determined the influence of likeability and similarity on source credibility and content evaluation, and identified similarity inflation bias as a conditional, mediated phenomenon.

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence, or AI, is becoming more and more common in Human Resource Management, or HRM. Organizations are using AI for activities such as recruitment, employee data analysis, scheduling, performance management, and employee support. These applications can help improve efficiency and also reduce the time spent on routine work. But at the same time, HRM is about people, relationships, emotions, and situations. These are things that cannot always be understood through data alone. This conceptual paper argues that the important question is not just whether AI can perform an HR activity. The question is whether it should perform that activity independently. The paper proposes a task-based framework. This framework looks at things such as how routine the activity is, how standardized it is, how much data it requires, its level of emotional complexity, interpersonal sensitivity, contextual ambiguity, and the potential impact on employees. Based on these characteristics, HR activities are broadly classified into three types: AI-dominant, human-dominant, or human-AI collaborative. Emotional Intelligence, or EI, is especially relevant for activities that involve emotional understanding, communication, conflict, and interpersonal judgment. The paper does not use primary empirical data. Instead, it develops conceptual propositions that can be examined through future empirical research. The framework adds to the discussion of AI-enabled HRM by connecting AI suitability with the emotional and interpersonal demands of HR work.

detail.abstract: Risky interactions in community messaging platforms often evolve through persistent contact, concentrated replies, repeated link sharing, conflict escalation, and disrupted group dynamics, making thread-level detection difficult using isolated messages, keywords, or noisy reports alone. We propose RiskThread-LF, a weakly supervised, privacy-preserving framework for detecting anomalous thread interactions and predicting credible negative feedback. The dataset contains 48.6 million message events, 6.2 million threads, 1.12 million communities, 27.4 million anonymous interaction edges, 3.1 million administrator actions, 960,000 reports, and 480,000 member-exit events. High-risk threads exhibit concentrated contact, repetitive dissemination, conflicting-reply propagation, or relational disruption, followed by credible signals including deletion, mute, warning, thread restriction, post-report intervention, member exit, or short-term disengagement; ordinary reports remain weak signals rather than ground truth. RiskThread-LF fuses reports, administrator actions, repeated propagation, abnormal reply concentration, member exits, and historical community benchmarks, while report-bias correction separates reporting probability from abnormal-propagation risk. The model achieves AUC=0.891 and Macro-F1=0.817, outperforming keyword rules, strong content-safety classifiers, long-context Transformers, temporal graph models, and LLM moderation. Early warning reaches AUPRC=0.734 and precedes credible negative feedback by 12.4 min on average. Removing weak-label fusion reduces Macro-F1 by 0.052, while removing report-bias correction increases FPR by 0.061 in highly reportactive communities. Under differential privacy (ε=3.0), AUC remains 0.862 and membership-inference success decreases from 0.214 to 0.128. These results demonstrate that reliable community-risk detection requires joint modeling of thread behavior, weak feedback, and reporting bias rather than text, keywords, or report counts alone.

title: Generative Engine Standardization and Autonomous Social Sanctioning

detail.title: Generative Engine Standardization and Autonomous Social Sanctioning

detail.abstract:
Two developments that are usually discussed separately became structurally coupled during 2025–2026. The first is generative engine standardization (GES): the rapid formalization of how autonomous systems access, verify, interpret, and transact with the open web — expressed through the IETF’s AI Preferences work, Content Credentials, the Model Context Protocol’s transfer to the Linux Foundation, agentic payment protocols, and the machine-readable marking duty in Article 50 of the EU AI Act, which becomes enforceable on 2 August 2026. The second is autonomous social sanctioning (ASN): the delegation of reputational penalty — de-citation, demotion, annotation, refusal, and revocation of access — to systems that act at machine speed, at population scale, and without contemporaneous human adjudication.

This paper argues that GES is not merely adjacent to ASN but is its enabling condition. Standardization produces a portable, machine-readable identity for every economic actor; once identity is portable, penalty becomes portable too. We assemble evidence from platform transparency data, a seven-month field study of AI-written Community Notes, three 2026 court decisions, network-level crawler telemetry, and two empirical audits of brand recommendation in large language models. We then advance five propositions about how the coupled regime behaves — most consequentially, that the returns to conformance decay toward zero as adoption becomes universal, while the penalty for non-conformance does not. We close with a measurement agenda, because the central problem of this regime is that its decisions are counted but its errors are not.

detail.abstract: The number of non-reported county yields by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) is increasing. This article explores factors that impact county corn and soybean yields that are not reported by USDA NASS. Factors such as county, land coverage, and average farm size are used to explain the likelihood of a yield being reported. We find that counties that have a high number of acres concentrated in a few farms may not have a NASS yield reported due to NASS reporting requirements.

detail.abstract: This Article develops interface law as a cross-doctrinal framework for analysing the consumer-facing interface as the evidentiary surface on which legal relations are increasingly formed, performed, and contested. Existing approaches-code as law, legal design, consumer-contract doctrine, privacy notices, and platform governance-each capture part of the phenomenon. None, however, treats the interface as the common site where heterogeneous obligations-contract notice, privacy disclosure, AI transparency, crypto-risk warnings, health-related disclaimers, child-safety notices, behavioural-steering controls, and jurisdictional claims-are presented to users and later assessed by courts, regulators, and counterparties. The Article's central claim is that screen-based legal communication changes the conditions under which legal obligations become visible, effective, disputable, and enforceable. Interface law identifies the analytical level at which those obligations become operative on screen. It also frames a jurisdictional problem that existing doctrines often obscure: when the relevant legal encounter occurs in a global, cross-border technological environment, should the interface be governed by the state of the entrepreneur, by the state of the user, or by cooperative rules that prevent national regulation from becoming a form of technological exclusion?

detail.abstract: The Global Market Portfolio (GMP) is the market-value-weighted sum of all assets investors collectively hold. This note reviews four recent GMP estimates (MSCI 2024; Goldman Sachs 2025; State Street 2026; Gadzinski, Schuller and Vacchino 2021) and reports half-century backtests (January 1976 to August 2026, monthly, USD) of an index built to the GMP's defining rule: hold the market as it is at each point in time, let weights float with prices, and reconstitute annually to reflect issuance. Three findings emerge. First, there is no single "GMP weight": the estimates agree on structure but differ by up to a factor of three in total size depending on definitional scope. Second, the GMP's significance lies in its weights not being chosen by anyone; both fixed-weight rebalancing and pure buy-and-hold depart from it. Third, over 50 years the floating, annually reconstituted index had the lowest volatility (8.05%) and lowest maximum drawdown of four diversified portfolios, and its Sharpe ratio (0.569) was statistically indistinguishable from those of a 60/40, an equal-thirds and a stock/gold portfolio; an equivalence test against 60/40 supports a claim of no material difference within roughly one percentage point a year. This neutrality is shared with other diversified portfolios; what is unique to the GMP is the provenance of its weights. Limitations, including unobservability, definitional dependence, and the exploratory nature of the backtests, are discussed.

title: Why the Stock Market is Resilient: An Adaptive Model of Corporate Self-financing

detail.title: Why the Stock Market is Resilient: An Adaptive Model of Corporate Self-financing

declarations.declarationOfInterest: no
declarations.funderStatement: no

detail.abstract:
Why does the stock market remain resilient, attract capital, and recover quickly from crises, even when aggregate returns are low and conventional metrics signal overvaluation? This paper uncovers a hidden, self-sustaining mechanism: the corporate self-financing cycle. When monetary policy raises the cost of capital, firms, most of which have belowunity betas, respond with share buybacks, compressing the equity denominator and mechanically restoring the aggregate return on equity (AROE). This is not financial engineering; it is an accounting-based defense mechanism rooted in the balance-sheet identity. 

      Using an ARDL model with Newey-West HAC estimation on U.S. nonfinancial corporate data (1985-2025), I provide empirical evidence for each phase of the cycle. Past merger volumes trigger buybacks; buybacks stabilize ROE; and, with a lag of four to five years, the capital returned to shareholders is redeployed into productive investments, generating growth in Gross Value Added. The cycle is synchronized by common exposure to the oscillation of the 3-month Treasury bill rate. 

      The findings challenge the narrative that buybacks are a form of "predatory value extraction." They suggest instead that the market is not a fragile mechanism but an adaptive, self-correcting system-one in which corporate managers act as silent stabilizers, and capital is continuously recycled to its most productive uses.

title: The Demographic Phillips Curve: Workforce Ageing, Cohort Replacement, and Wage Inflation Dynamics

detail.abstract: The slope of the Phillips curve has declined markedly across advanced economies since the 1990s, yet there is no consensus on why this relationship has weakened. Existing explanations emphasize central bank credibility, globalization, and the measurement of labour market slack. This article argues that demographic change provides a complementary perspective that has received comparatively little attention. It synthesizes insights from population economics, labour economics, and macroeconomics the Demographic Phillips Curve, in which workforce ageing influences the aggregate wage Phillips curve through three mechanisms. First, older workers exhibit lower wage cyclicality, altering the aggregate wage response through changes in workforce composition. Second, cohort replacement reshapes inflation expectations because successive generations accumulate different inflation experiences over the life cycle. Third, demographic change may introduce composition bias into conventional estimates of the NAIRU by altering the age structure of employment and unemployment. Together, these mechanisms suggest that demographic transition may influence the estimated slope, intercept, and expectations component of the aggregate Phillips curve alongside more established explanations. The article outlines a research agenda for identifying and quantifying these demographic effects, including the development of demographically adjusted measures of labour market slack and comparative analyses across countries at different stages of demographic transition. It concludes by discussing the implications for future empirical research and monetary policy in ageing economies.

detail.abstract: A recent Science article "China's Solar Expansion Policy Reduces Bird Diversity" by Zhang et al. (2026) shows that the stringency of China's policies promoting solar photovoltaics has a negative impact on bird diversity. We revisit this issue and conclude that there is no evidence of this being the case. If we assume that Zhang et al.'s (2026) data treatment is true and fair, then they have ignored the fact that fences around solar farms can deny birdwatching access, mechanically causing observed bird diversity to decline. However, and more importantly, the negative link between bird diversity and solar photovoltaic policy stringency claimed in Zhang et al. (2026) is likely due to missing-data treatment-setting miss values to zero. Without setting missing values to zero, the correlation between solar photovoltaic policy intensity and solar photovoltaic activities is negative, invalidating their policy stringency measure. Note that 54.60% (43.91%) of observations have missing values for AREA (PSI) and they are set to zero. Further, the solar photovoltaic policy stringency index appears to be based on current-year newly issued policy documents when it should be based on a stock of temporal cumulative policy documents, causing the measure to lose its relevance and become inconsistent with reality. The negative link between bird diversity and China's solar photovoltaic endeavor disappears when correct data are used. Our analysis is important as Zhang et al.'s (2026) conclusion can potentially misguide sustainability efforts and energy policies in China as well as the rest of the world.

detail.abstract:
Design/methodology/approach. The sample comprises 63,858 firm-year observations on 9,983 Italian innovative start-ups, innovative SMEs and ordinary SMEs between 2015 and 2024, drawn from statutory accounts. The collection period is regressed on bank debt with firm and year effects under nine estimators and six alternative scalings of both sides of the equation. A cluster analysis comparing six algorithms across eleven validity indices partitions the firms by financial configuration, and the equation is re-estimated within each group. Six regression learners fitted to the same demeaned data test the linearity and additivity restrictions the panel imposes.
Purpose. Trade credit and bank credit have been described as substitutes for three decades, yet a competing tradition finds them complementary, and the evidence has not converged. This paper argues that the disagreement is definitional rather than empirical. Almost every study measures trade credit received, treating the firm as a borrower choosing between two funding sources, while the credit the firm extends to its own customers enters as a control or not at all. The paper estimates both margins on one sample and asks whether bank borrowing lengthens or shortens the credit small and medium enterprises grant.
Findings. Bank indebtedness and the collection period move together within firms, at 0.48 days per percentage point of bank debt over turnover and positive under every estimator, while the same equation on payables returns −0.43. A model of a supplier facing a bank credit limit generates both signs from one first-order condition and bounds pass-through between zero and one, which the data satisfy at 0.126 euro per euro. The association reaches 0.81 among long-cycle firms, halves where liquidity is abundant, and declines from 0.80 to 0.50 across the decade as bank credit loosens.
Originality/value. The paper reconciles two literatures previously read as contradictory by estimating both margins of trade credit on one sample and deriving both signs from a single decision problem. It identifies a measurement problem the field has not addressed: because trade credit granted and bank debt are conventionally scaled by turnover, the estimated coefficient ranges from +0.48 to −0.12 across ratio specifications, so published estimates are not mutually comparable. It is also the first study of trade credit supply in the certified Italian populations of innovative start-ups and SMEs.

detail.abstract: The American Medical Association's development of a proposed coding framework for Clinically Meaningful Algorithmic Analyses (CMAA) has generated concern among nurses. The prospect that autonomous artificial intelligence-enabled analyses could receive dist inct coding recognition while registered nursing work remains financially obscured within facility payments exposes a longstanding inconsistency in health care payment policy. Nursing assessment, surveillance, clinical judgment, education, advocacy, and ca re coordination produce clinically meaningful information and improve patient outcomes, yet this work generally lacks independent payment recognition. This paper challenges the assumption, however, that parallel billing codes are nursing's best path to eco nomic recognition. Creating nursing-specific billing codes could make selected nursing services more visible, but billing alone would not capture the full value of relational and preventive nursing care, guarantee additional resources, or ensure that resul ting revenue is reinvested in nursing. We propose a broader agenda centered on governing the AI dividend-both the net financial gains attributable to AI and the clinical capacity released after accounting for the new work AI creates. Nursing should support effective AI while demanding financial transparency, workforce reinvestment, retain-and-retrain protections, formal nursing authority in AI governance, and payment policies that directly incentivize investment in the nursing workforce. Nursing's strategic objective should not be simply to generate more billable units, but to ensure that payment policy sustains the human capacity on which safe and meaningful care depends.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a theory of alpha decay for quantitative-finance signals whose construction is public, reproducible, and economically implementable. The central claim is deliberately narrower than the statement that every open-source model has zero alpha. A public signal may retain conditional or temporary predictive content, but its net implementable alpha should tend to decline as information diffuses, capital crowds the trade, arbitrage compresses mispricing, execution costs consume gross returns, and the market regime changes. We formalize this intuition with a public-signal state variable, a capital-crowding process, a cost function, and a regime-survival process. The resulting model yields an alpha half-life and a break-even time at which expected net alpha reaches zero. We derive propositions showing when public disclosure necessarily lowers net alpha and when alpha can survive through capacity, latency, non-public data, changing implementation, or structural compensation for risk. We then propose an empirical design based on publication-date event studies, rolling out-of-sample tests, survival analysis, multiple-testing corrections, and cost-aware portfolio construction. The paper does not assert that all Kalman filters, Bayesian models, or open-source strategies have no alpha; it argues that public availability is an economically meaningful mechanism that makes persistent, cost-adjusted alpha a demanding empirical claim.

The study is a retrospective audit of the author's own tooling and of an earlier generalisation the author made about it, which is withdrawn here; no third party commissioned, funded or reviewed it. detail.abstract:
This retrospective forensic case study audits one production parameter-search pipeline for a
cryptocurrency market maker against 20 runs, 60 token-level decisions, and 52 MB of retained
artifacts. It begins by refuting the claim that motivated it: the search does not always adopt its
fitted maximum. It kept the live configuration in 37 of 60 decisions, and its out-of-sample guard
demonstrably rejects a worse fitted winner. The generalisation that provoked the audit — that an
automated search over a noisy trading objective reports confident adoptions from pure noise — is
false about this tool and is withdrawn.

Four defects were found elsewhere in the pipeline. A swept parameter that the execution engine
ignored produced a perfectly monotone and entirely meaningless response surface. A narrow ladder
sweep let a single outlier present as a strong parameter effect. Independent-error assumptions
applied to overlapping windows doubled the apparent number of threshold crossings. And a validator
checking nominal notional passed a configuration whose pre-trade rejections were, without
exception, on one side. In each incident the defective measurement made the pipeline's output look cleaner
or more actionable than the repaired measurement did.

A fifth proposed incident — an objective apparently pinned at an infeasibility ceiling — is
withdrawn. The objective is gradient-ordered by design, and the retained artifacts cannot
reconstruct the full evaluation population; they support exact counts only at named scopes, and the
paper states which.

The audit separately finds that all 12 adoptions carrying a retained out-of-sample profit figure
adopt a loss, despite the tool's relative-to-baseline guard functioning correctly. That is a
labelling and operator-action problem rather than evidence that automated search is unsound.

These incidents were selected retrospectively from one pipeline after discovery. They do not
estimate how often search-pipeline defects occur, nor establish that such defects are generally
biased toward confidence. They motivate a mechanism hypothesis — that some broken measurements
reduce observed variance or suppress contradictory structure, so that failure resembles signal —
and testing it would require a prospective incident sample or a controlled known-null mutation
study, neither of which this paper has.

detail.abstract: Europe's Long-Term Transmission Rights (LTTR) scheme systematically transfers congestion income from Transmission System Operators (TSOs) to holders. While ACER (2024) finds the rights underpriced against contemporaneous forward spreads, the prohibition of reserve prices under current regulation forces the FCA 2.0 review to consider reducing auction volumes. This paper quantifies the transfer, maps its concentration, and tests the efficacy of this proposed remedy. Reconstructing the transfer direction-by-direction from JAO auction results and ENTSO-E hourly prices, we verify our method against the regulator's aggregate data within 1% on both gross components and 2.2% on the net. Our dataset covers 74 cleared directional instruments across 38 border pairs from 2019 to mid-2026. The net transfer over that window is €4.85 billion, holders paid €20.24 billion and got €25.09 billion, a 24% aggregate return, over the window, on what they paid. The transfer is concentrated: ten directions account for 90% of the €4.85 billion transferred to holders. The transfer is not confined to the crisis but persistent: the monthly product, the shortest horizon in the product set, transferred value to holders in every year of the window. Volume reduction does not significantly raise auction prices. Re-clearing submitted bid schedules reveals a demand curve that is nearly flat; a 30% volume cut raises prices by only a few percent, and deeper cuts required for material price increases would eliminate most of the instrument's value. The findings suggest volume reduction lever cannot correct the price, and the constraint that forecloses price formation lies outside the implementing act's reach.

title: Common versus Private Information in Threshold Public Good Provision

detail.title: Common versus Private Information in Threshold Public Good Provision

detail.abstract: We study a threshold public good game à la Palfrey and Rosenthal (1984) in which it is uncertain whether the good is valuable, and citizens observe informative signals about its value. Our focus is on comparing two information structures — private and common information — in terms of the expected utility they generate in symmetric equilibrium. The comparison is particularly stark in the two polar cases. In the volunteer's dilemma, private information weakly dominates common information for all participation costs, whereas in the weakest-link case the opposite ranking holds. For interior provision thresholds, the comparison depends on the cost of participation. Common information is preferred at sufficiently low costs, while private information may become preferable as participation becomes more costly, with at most two reversals in the welfare ranking. Moreover, increasing the provision threshold systematically shifts the comparison in favor of common information. Finally, we study large societies and show that the comparison becomes increasingly sharp depending on whether the required participation rate lies below or above the expected share of favorable signals when the public good is valuable.

detail.abstract: This paper propose a sensitivity analysis approach for general likelihood-based models. A synthetic confounder is constructed via simulation which has pre-specified partial correlations with the residualised treatment and outcome variables, thus capturing researchers' beliefs about the strength of the confounding. By including the synthetic confounder in the short (misspecified) model, the framework yields exact adjusted average marginal effects. Further, it is possible to calculate fragility thresholds via a bisection algorithm and includes a benchmarking procedure to calibrate the sensitivity parameters against observed covariates. A Monte Carlo simulation shows that the new framework outperforms direct application of existing sensitivity approaches for linear models under moderate to strong confounding. The new framework is applied the 1970 British Cohort Study to evaluate the sensitivity of the effect of early life cognitive skills on labour market participation and job quality during adulthood.

detail.abstract:
Background. Public football-linked records are routinely pooled under shared names before the research object is specified (Wong, 2026a). Head-to-head (H2H) pages make the pooling vivid: one tab label is read as one historical record that then authorises talk about tonight.

Objectives. This article documents how public pre-match score and preview surfaces instantiate bounded objects. It asks (i) which objects sit under H2H/form widgets; (ii) where listed meetings are already joined to tonight on the score site; and (iii) whether off-page news and club prose move with those widgets as kick-off nears.

Methods. Three unplayed fixtures missing a same-season club H2H were archived before kick-off on Jiebao, SofaScore, and Flashscore. Competition-phase Tc timestamps the cited row; observation-time To timestamps the capture relative to tonight’s kick-off. Ipswich Town v Liverpool (Premier League, 4 September 2026) is the complete dual-layer exhibit. Toulouse v Lille (Ligue 1) and Real Sociedad v Celta (La Liga) replicate the three-site interface. The unit is a dated public module bound to one fixture envelope R_now. Frozen Kk permission ticks are an appendix inventory, not the dependent variable.

Results. Across cases, Flashscore’s first H2H slice is completed meetings only. SofaScore’s first slice places a future meeting and the current unplayed fixture inside the H2H carousel. Jiebao keeps a mixed-season historical footer beside media copy that already speaks to tonight. In the Premier League case those interface assignments persist into the last six hours, while BBC Sport, Sky Sports, and club items appear. Repeating an existing preview family is not a new narrative event.

Conclusions. Public H2H and narrative are related by join and non-identity, not by a single updating record. Comparability of labels is not portability of objects (Wong, 2026c). The study does not test who wins, whether H2H is substantively true, or whether independent readers recover a coding key.

detail.abstract: How does a five-business-day ownership-disclosure deadline operate in practice? Using 73,048 EDINET documents from 2021-2026, I reconstruct 63,682 filing events after consolidating amendment chains. In the 36,461-event regular-filing sample under General Reporting, 45.04% of events were filed on the fifth business day. Yet the equal-weighted mean of filer-specific fifth-day rates was 27.57%. The 17.47-percentage-point gap equals the covariance between each filer's number of filings and fifth-day filing rate divided by the mean number of filings; the two metrics therefore capture distinct estimands-the composition of the filing flow and the average filing propensity across filers. I also link initial reports to subsequent Change Reports. Among 4,482 timely initial filings satisfying the inclusion rule, 151 (3.37%) were associated with a comparable increase in holdings that triggered another reporting obligation before the initial filing. The median additional change in the ownership ratio was 1.26 percentage points, and the median interval between obligation-trigger dates was two business days. This descriptive study is conditional on observed filings and does not identify unfiled obligations, causal effects of the deadline, or filer motives. Evaluations of disclosure regimes should distinguish filings from filers, deadline-day filing from late filing, and legal timeliness from whether holdings changed again before filing.

detail.abstract: When a language-model valuation pipeline retracts an invalid input, which visible component of the record it leaves behind continues to transmit that input's influence? In a preregistered transcript-ablation experiment on three commercial model endpoints and 30 fictional firms, an upstream call receives a randomized high or low external fair-value anchor; its valuation and sterilized rationale are frozen and replayed in nine controlled forms to independent downstream calls after the source is declared invalid. The prior estimate, replayed alone after withdrawal (in two of three cohorts usually the anchor's own digits, copied upstream), carries a high-low difference of 0.027 of the clean center relative to a byte-identical redacted control, about 6% of the upstream anchoring effect, and disclosing its tainted lineage did not detectably reduce that carrier. In estimation-only contrasts, replaying the full record as the model's own earlier turn rather than inline raises its carrier from 0.038 to 0.091, whereas leaving the withdrawn source sentence visible beside the correction reduces it. An exploratory extension on three firm pairs estimates that retraction removes roughly 85% of what the un-withdrawn record would carry; per hop, the withdrawn number transmits 0.06 of an upstream perturbation and the un-withdrawn record 0.40. The pattern is a representation effect, not a provenance effect: downstream calls respond to how a prior conclusion is displayed, not to what they are told about it. For multi-agent financial workflows, disclosure alone does not detectably reduce transmission; controls must also govern how prior conclusions are represented in the visible record.

detail.abstract: This paper presents a model of the activity of patent intermediaries and potential infringers in a system of costly patent litigation. Because the intermediary, in comparison to the inventor, has a more credible threat to sue, both the revenue from infringement litigation and the intrinsic value of the patent are greater in the intermediary's hands. The central finding is that intermediaries license patents to potential infringers when infringement litigation is inefficient. Intermediaries tend to acquire high-quality patents from inventors and assign low-quality patents to potential infringers. Another issue this model addresses is the differential between the private and the social value of patents. Infringement reduces the private value of a patent but can increase the social value. This distinction implies that private and social incentives to license or to litigate patents may diverge. Intermediaries benefit society by licensing socially inefficient patents.

detail.abstract: We study the role of officeholders in the formation of political preferences during childhood. We also document lasting impacts on primary participation and survey-based attitudes. The effects are systematically stronger in settings where governors enjoy greater institutional authority, especially over education and budgeting, and when they are more popular.

detail.abstract: In May 2026 the Government of India approved a support scheme for the industrial gasification of coal and lignite (about USD 3.9 billion), targeting 100 million tonnes by 2030. title: AttenIR: Aligning Dense Visual Attention with Mesh Warping for Unsupervised Image Retargeting

detail.title: AttenIR: Aligning Dense Visual Attention with Mesh Warping for Unsupervised Image Retargeting
detail.abstract: Image retargeting aims to resize images while preserving salient content free from distortion and stretching. Recent learning-based solutions reduce reliance on traditional hand-crafted features and optimization procedures, leading to more efficient and generalizable performance. Nevertheless, existing approaches still struggle to preserve global structure and content fidelity. To address these limitations, we propose AttenIR, an unsupervised image retargeting framework requiring no manual labels, based on content-aware mesh warping, which effectively couples dense visual attention with sparse mesh constraints. We formulate the mesh deformation as a vertex displacement regression task. Guided by saliency priors, our method jointly optimizes scale, structure, and geometry preservation losses. By combining dense visual attention with semantic features, it achieves robust, unsupervised retargeting without manual annotations. Our primary contributions include (1) a lightweight unsupervised method for image retargeting that ensures content fidelity and preserves global structure, and (2) a coarse-to-fine projection strategy to align dense visual attention priors with sparse mesh constraints, enabling content-aware deformation at the pixel level. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves competitive and superior performance compared with both traditional and state-of-the-art learning-based methods.

detail.abstract: Trading firms routinely pay departing employees to sit out of the market for six months to two years under garden leave and noncompete arrangements, at a privately contracted rate ranging from base salary-the customary minimum, commonly $150,000-$200,000 per year-up to full compensation. This proposal asks what that money buys. Two motives are observationally similar but carry opposite welfare implications: firms may be protecting proprietary knowledge until it depreciates, an appropriability mechanism that sustains innovation incentives; or they may be paying to deny rivals access to scarce talent itself, a form of upstream foreclosure that misallocates human capital. I develop a contract-design model in which a departing worker carries two assets-firm-specific knowledge that decays at a strategy-specific rate and general ability that does not-and show that the two motives leave distinct fingerprints on observable contract features. The motive is identified not from exclusion length alone but from how contract design responds to knowledge half-life, rival demand, and destination: protection predicts sitout lengths that track knowledge half-lives; blocking predicts lengths pinned at legal maxima, insensitive to knowledge decay, escalating with rival entry, and targeted at competitor-bound moves. The financial trading industry is the unique setting in which these design features are observable: regulatory personnel registers measure realized sit-outs and destinations at the person level, alpha-decay rates vary sharply and measurably across strategy classes, and the price of exclusion-heterogeneous across firms and workers, and only partially disclosedis bounded below by posted base salaries and observed in structure through litigation and disclosure records, with its heterogeneity itself supplying an additional testable prediction. The empirical design combines register-based gap panels, entity-level strategy classification, fundentry threat measures, and policy events in the UK, New York, and California to separate the two mechanisms and to inform the contested regulation of noncompete agreements.

detail.title: Modalities Should Talk to Each Other: Dual-Stream Multimodal Learning for Long-Horizon Influenza Forecasting
detail.abstract: Forecasting long-range influenza-like illness (ILI) matters for public health readiness. Publicly available surveillance datasets typically pair numeric epidemiological signals with textual information that is noisy, loosely structured, only indirectly related to near-term trends, and often lagged relative to the numeric signal. Fusing the two therefore requires careful design. We propose Dual-Stream Attention (DSA), a multimodal deep learning framework that forecasts 12-week-ahead ILI activity from a 36-week multimodal history by letting the numerical and textual streams condition each other. Using the Time-MMD health-domain dataset, DSA separately encodes the two modalities with a Transformer-based numerical encoder and a domain-adapted headline encoder, then couples them through a bidirectional Cross-Modal Attention (CMA) mechanism: the text (news headlines) conditions the interpretation of the numeric signal and vice versa. The CMA output then passes to a causal temporal model for forecasting. Evaluated across ten random seeds, DSA achieves a median test MSE of 0.416, versus 0.668, 0.607, and 0.851 for iTransformer, TaTS, and GPT4MTS – mean-error reductions of 54.95%, 37.29%, and 67.23%, with paired Cohen’s 𝑑 of 0.555, 0.337, and 0.345 – and ranks first in 100% of bootstrap draws. It also has substantially lower worst-window error than all baselines. On an external-geography dataset, DSA again ranks first among nine evaluated baselines. Ablations show the advantage does not depend on text-encoder choice or language-model finetuning, and that bidirectional attention outperforms either direction alone. Finally, perturbation-based faithfulness analysis shows the learned CMA is functionally informative under targeted masking, with a stronger effect in the text-to-numerical direction.

detail.abstract: The paper examines how digitalization affects the cost and organization of cross-border personal remittances and how these changes relate to a broader restructuring of the global payment and financial architecture. Drawing on transparent observations from the World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide (RPW) database for 2011-2025 and the official aggregates of Issue 53, it shows that the average cost of sending USD 200 fell from 8.86% in 2011 to 6.49% in Q1 2025 (-26.8%), although the decline slowed markedly after 2021. detail.abstract:
Agentic trading systems are usually evaluated by the accuracy of individual forecasts. That evaluation misses a distinct systemic-risk channel: several agents can be individually well calibrated while forming correlated posterior beliefs and submitting synchronized orders. We develop a controlled market experiment that holds marginal predictive accuracy approximately constant and varies information overlap, common posterior calibration error, and the homogeneity of risk controls. Agents report auditable posterior probabilities over calm, turbulent, and crisis states. Their orders clear in a market where one-sided flow consumes depth and affects subsequent prices and observations. 
The identifying comparison is therefore not AI versus non-AI. It is low versus high cross-agent belief dependence conditional on comparable individual forecast quality. The mechanism predicts a temporal sequence from posterior dependence to order synchronization, depth depletion, price impact, and tail volatility. A randomized independent-execution placebo preserves correlated beliefs while breaking the belief-to-trade timing channel. In the pilot mechanism experiment, accuracy-matched high-dependence agents produce sharply higher order synchronization, realized variance, tail returns, and a spread/depth proxy, whereas the placebo returns close to the independent benchmark. These results are mechanism validation, not evidence about any particular language model. The evidence is deliberately architectural: it establishes the mechanism in a controlled synthetic market and does not estimate the prevalence or aggregate effect of deployed commercial systems.

detail.abstract: Younger generations express increasing concern for environmental sustainability, yet little is known about how sustainability considerations shape labour supply and worker sorting. We study the value workers place on green job attributes and the behavioural motives underlying these preferences. Using a preregistered discrete choice experiment with a representative sample of 2,008 Italian young adults, we estimate willingness to pay for environmentally sustainable job characteristics, including green products and production processes, environmental training, sustainability certifications, green fringe benefits, and sustainability-linked incentives. We find that workers are willing to forgo between 2% and 8% of monthly wages to obtain specific green job attributes, magnitudes comparable to those associated with established job amenities. To assess external validity, we link experimentally elicited preferences to actual educational choices and show that individuals with stronger green preferences are more likely to enrol in university programmes providing green skills. We further find that green preferences are strongly associated with prosociality, only weakly related to patience, and unrelated to risk tolerance. Our results identify environmental sustainability as a distinct dimension of job quality that may influence worker sorting and firms' ability to attract talent.

detail.abstract: This study develops a comprehensive index to assess the quality of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reporting by European banks, focusing on early adoption of sustainability reporting standards. It examines whether reporting quality is associated with governance mechanisms-specifically the existence of an ESG committee, the inclusion of climate-related targets in remuneration, and board gender diversity-as well as institutional affiliations, namely membership in the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF) and the Net-Zero Banking Alliance (NZBA). The study also evaluates changes in actual GHG emissions to assess whether disclosure requirements are accompanied by substantive outcomes. Results indicate that 65% of banks reporting financed emissions achieved an average reduction of 20%. Regression analysis reveals that climate-linked remuneration is positively associated with reporting quality, consistent with Agency Theory. Board gender diversity is also significant, aligning with both Agency Theory and Upper Echelons Theory. Furthermore, membership in PCAF and the NZBA is positively related to reporting quality, consistent with Institutional Theory. These findings advance the accounting literature on environmental disclosures by identifying governance and institutional determinants of reporting quality and provide insights for regulators, standard setters, and practitioners seeking to enhance climaterelated reporting practices.

title: Systems, Boundaries, and Belonging: From General Systems Theory to an Ontology of Organized Existence

detail.title: Systems, Boundaries, and Belonging: From General Systems Theory to an Ontology of Organized Existence

detail.abstract:
This article examines the relationship between systems theory and the Philosophy of Belonging and argues that, although the two approaches share a rejection of atomistic reductionism and an emphasis on organization, relations, boundaries, and differentiation, they operate at different explanatory levels. Beginning with Ludwig von Bertalanffy’s General System Theory, Kenneth E. Boulding’s hierarchy of systemic complexity, and Niklas Luhmann’s theory of self-referential social systems, the article asks whether systems theory provides an ontology of organized existence or instead presupposes the organization that such an ontology must explain.

The Philosophy of Belonging addresses this question through the proposition Being is Belonging. Systems are interpreted as particular configurations of belonging rather than as ontologically primitive entities. The article develops this distinction through the concepts of imperfect belonging, synchrony and diachrony, emergence, observer-independent and reflexively constituted belonging, and the stratification of reality into material, biological, and institutional-human forms of organized existence.

Particular attention is given to the distinction between systemic complexity and ontological stratification. Increasing complexity is understood as the emergence of new forms and functions requiring additional explanatory categories, without implying superiority, teleology, or greater evolutionary fitness. The article also distinguishes emergence within a stratum from emergence between strata and argues that the institutional-human stratum introduces reflexivity as an additional organizational capacity through which forms of belonging can become objects of representation, criticism, and deliberate transformation.

The article concludes that systems theory provides indispensable models for understanding organized relations, while the Philosophy of Belonging addresses the more general ontological question of what makes organized existence possible. Systems theory asks how organized wholes operate; the Philosophy of Belonging asks what it means for anything organized to exist.

detail.abstract:
This article develops a jurisprudential account of delegation to stochastic decision architectures. Existing work on automated public decision-making has already established that algorithmic systems can disrupt familiar doctrines of delegation, discretion, accountability, and administrative responsibility. The unresolved problem addressed here is narrower. A generative or otherwise stochastic system may be institutionally authorized even though, under fixed legally relevant inputs, its operative procedure can instantiate more than one legally consequential output. The legal question is therefore not exhausted by asking whether authority was delegated to an algorithm, whether a human remains nominally in the loop, or whether the system is explainable. It is whether authorization of the decision-generating architecture entails authorization of each particular output that the architecture can produce.

The paper calls the discontinuity between these two levels the Distributional Authorization Gap. Let G denote an authorized generative procedure composed of a model M, a selection or decoding rule S, and institutional constraints C. For legally relevant input X, G induces a distribution P(O | X; G) over possible outputs. Institutional authorization of G does not, without a further rule of legal imputation, entail legal authorization of every oᵢ in the support of that distribution. This proposition is especially important where two technically valid executions under materially identical facts and law can produce legally non-equivalent outcomes, such as grant and denial, detention and release, eligibility and ineligibility, or sanction and non-sanction.

The argument is analytical rather than empirical. It reconstructs the presuppositions of delegation theory around identifiable authority, institutional continuity, imputability, and bounded competence; distinguishes the present problem from established debates on algorithmic delegation, randomness, discretion, and predictive uncertainty; and identifies the point at which stochastic generation changes the object that must be legally authorized. The paper does not claim that randomization is inherently unlawful, that all machine-learning systems are stochastic at inference, or that legal decision-making has historically required deterministic reasoning. Law has long used lotteries, probabilistic evidence, structured discretion, and decision under uncertainty. The distinctive problem arises when an institution authorizes a generative procedure whose output space includes legally incompatible realizations without specifying why the realization actually sampled, rather than another equally procedurally available realization, counts as the institution's authorized act.

The article therefore reframes stochastic delegation as a problem of output-level validity. Its central claim is that architecture-level authorization and output-level authorization are analytically distinct and that legal systems require an explicit bridge between them. That bridge may be supplied by bounded output design, a legally specified selection rule, meaningful human ratification, reviewable reasons, or another institutional rule of imputation. Where no such bridge exists, the system may be technically authorized while the legal status of its instantiated decision remains underdetermined.

detail.abstract: As deployed LLM systems serve increasing query volumes, inference energy becomes an important component of total AI energy consumption. Practitioners face a recurring decision: improve accuracy by scaling to a larger model, or by applying prompting strategies such as chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning or few-shot exemplars. Both options increase computational cost, but their energy-accuracy trade-offs are poorly characterized. In this paper, GPU inference energy for 9 open-source LLMs spanning 5 model families (0.5B-14.7B parameters) across 5 standardised benchmarks was measured, comparing direct (0-shot) inference against enhanced prompting strategies (8-shot CoT for mathematical reasoning; few-shot exemplars for other tasks). Using real power telemetry from an NVIDIA A100 GPU, accuracy-energy Pareto frontiers for each benchmark were constructed, and it was observed that 56-72% of tested model-strategy configurations are energy-dominated, meaning a strictly cheaper and more accurate alternative exists. When enhanced prompting appears on the Pareto frontier, it does so primarily at the upper end of the accuracy range, where direct prompting among the evaluated models does not reach the same accuracy. On two of five benchmarks (MMLU and HellaSwag), no enhanced prompting configuration reaches the frontier at all. Further, it was observed that model family selection can have a larger effect on energy efficiency than prompting strategy: in some cases, a smaller model from one family dominates a larger model from another on both accuracy and energy. These results suggest that energy-aware model selection can often reduce inference energy relative to applying enhanced prompting by default. This analysis is limited to open-weight models up to 14.7B parameters on a single GPU platform and should be validated at larger scales and on production serving infrastructure.

detail.abstract: We develop an efficient Monte Carlo simulation scheme for pricing options under the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck driven stochastic volatility model via the operator splitting approach. We performed numerical tests to compare accuracy-speed performance of pricing options using our operator splitting scheme with these three pioneering schemes. We found that our scheme competes favorably well in terms of accuracy-speed tradeoff among all these schemes, in particular for pricing path dependent options with a large number of monitoring instants. The performance of our scheme can be well enhanced by martingale-preserving control variates and variance reduction via conditioning.

detail.abstract:
Perception-based governance indicators are central to empirical development research, but their published standard errors are rarely used to evaluate within country movements. This paper proposes a simple diagnostic for annual index change: each country-year movement is decomposed into raw score change, producer-reported uncertainty, and a standardized signal-to-noise statistic. The method is applied to two leading corruption measures, the WorldBank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators Control of Corruption measure and Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index.
Using the 2020 suspension of the World Bank’s Doing Business report as a calendar reference point, the paper documents a sharp producer asymmetry. After 2020, both indicators shift toward more negative mean annual changes and both report lower pooled standard errors. Yet they diverge in the evidence content of annual movements: WGI-Control of Corruption records a decline in absolute standardized movement, while CPI records an increase. The contrast is not driven by scale, country coverage, Russia–Ukraine war cases, or the exact cutoff year. Additional checks show that the WGI-side pattern extends across most WGI pillars, while the CPI precision tightening is not concentrated in countries with initially low source counts.
The results do not identify a causal effect of the Doing Business controversy. Instead, they show that two corruption indicators often treated as substitutes translate annual governance movements into different amounts of statistical evidence once producer-reported uncertainty is incorporated. This matters for applied research using corruption indicators to measure institutional change.

Using more than 30 million birth records from 1970 to 2000, I link mothers’ states and years of birth to differential exposure to the DDT expansion. The empirical design exploits the rapid post-1945 expansion of DDT and predetermined cross-state variation in pre-DDT cotton intensity. I find that greater maternal early-life exposure reduced offspring birth weight by 17.9 grams and increased low birth weight and small for gestational age by 9.2 and 10.6 percent relative to their means. Gestational length and preterm birth were largely unaffected, indicating that the intergenerational effects were concentrated in fetal growth. Additional evidence shows that exposed cohorts experienced lower educational attainment, income, and employment, greater disability, and higher mortality later in life. Complementary evidence from the later cancellation of DDT shows improvements in several birth outcomes as exposure declined. The findings demonstrate that environmental exposures can have health consequences extending to the next generation.

detail.abstract: This paper examines what share of emerging-market equities should be added to a world portfolio from the perspective of a euro-based investor. The analysis rests on the euro-denominated monthly returns of two accumulating index funds over ten years (August 2016 to August 2026): the iShares Core MSCI World UCITS ETF (IE00B4L5Y983) as the world portfolio and the iShares MSCI EM UCITS ETF (IE00B4L5YC18) as the emerging-market holding; the risk-free rate is set at 2 per cent. The paper introduces the asset class: the origin of the term and the classification schemes, the criteria for promotion to developed status, the largest emerging markets by economic weight and by market capitalisation, and their sensitivity to US interest rates, their public debt and their currency risks. The Markowitz minimum-variance portfolio holds 37.9 per cent emerging markets (volatility 12.46 per cent, return 11.58 per cent p.a.). The tangency portfolio of the capital market line contains no emerging-market equities ex post (minus 2.5 per cent unconstrained), because the world fund earned 12.92 per cent p.a. at 13.25 per cent volatility, a Sharpe ratio of 0.82, whereas the emerging-market fund earned 9.40 per cent at 14.47 per cent volatility, a Sharpe ratio of only 0.51. The market portfolio with 11.8 per cent emerging markets falls short of the maximum Sharpe ratio by only 0.006. A Black-Litterman optimisation with empirically estimated interest-rate views yields an allocation of 25.7 per cent (range 22 to 29 per cent) if the US one-year rate falls by 1.5 percentage points and an allocation of zero if it rises by 1.5 percentage points. The allocation is therefore a rate-dependent corridor from zero to about 25 per cent around the market weight of twelve per cent.

detail.abstract: Neurotechnology has moved from clinical laboratories into consumer wearables, workplace monitoring systems, and forensic practice, yet the legal protection of mental states remains fragmented across incompatible regulatory pathways. This article identifies and names that fragmentation as the "pathway-dependence problem": constitutional and statutory protection for the mind is triggered not by the value genuinely at stake-freedom of thought and the integrity of one's own cognitive processes-but by whichever technological or doctrinal channel an intervention happens to travel through, such as personal-data processing, a listed "AI system," or a formal medical procedure. Interventions that alter, infer, or access mental states outside these recognized channels fall through the gaps of every regime examined. Using a comparative methodology across Chile's constitutionalized neurorights and 2023 Emotiv jurisprudence, Brazil's sub-national mental-integrity amendment and pending federal reform, United States state-level neural-data privacy statutes (Colorado, California), the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act prohibited-practices regime, and UNESCO's 2025 Recommendation on the Ethics of Neurotechnology, the article demonstrates that each instrument protects the mind only derivatively, through data-protection, consumer-protection, or AI-classification doctrine. It argues that this indirection is not incidental but structural, and that it produces predictable coverage gaps wherever cognitive interference occurs without generating "data," without using a classified "AI system," or without medical framing. The article's original contribution is doctrinal: it isolates pathway-dependence as a discrete failure mode distinct from the transparency, bias, and consent problems that dominate the neurorights literature, and proposes a Pathway-Neutral Cognitive Liberty Standard keyed directly to the constitutional interest in mental self-determination rather than to the instrumentality used to reach it.

detail.abstract: This paper develops financial conditions indices that target macroeconomic tail risk. The resulting index is specific to both the macroeconomic target and the quantile of interest.
